title: Filtering engine v1: include/exclude rules + field allowlist; document filter semantics
author: Diego Santos
release_notes: Adds filter engine v1 for audit export destinations (include/exclude + allowlisted fields). No behavior change unless destination filtering is configured.
body:
Context: SIEM-ready audit export requires customer-configurable filtering to reduce downstream noise/cost, but we need predictable semantics and strict controls around what can be filtered (avoid accidental PII-based targeting).

This PR implements filtering engine v1 in audit-log-exporter and documents the stable semantics we expect to support in beta. The engine compiles a FilterSpec into a predicate and is used by the worker prior to sink batching.

What’s included:
- FilterSpec model with include/exclude rules (destination-scoped)
- Deterministic evaluation semantics (documented + unit tested)
- Field allowlist + validation (reject unknown fields, reject disallowed fields)
- Match operators: exact match + prefix match for select fields (event_type + resource.type)
- Normalization rules (trim, lowercasing for enum-like fields)
- Documentation: config examples, operator precedence, and guidance on duplicates/at-least-once interaction

Semantics (v1):
- If no include rules are specified => include all events (subject to exclude rules).
- If include rules exist => event must match at least one include rule to be kept.
- Exclude rules are always applied last; if event matches any exclude rule, it is dropped.
- Within a rule: all specified fields must match (AND across fields).
- Within a field: multiple values are OR’ed.
- Unknown fields or unsupported operators are validation errors at config-parse time (destination goes to FAILED_VALIDATION in control plane; exporter refuses to start that destination).

Allowlisted filter fields (v1):
- event.type (supports exact + prefix, e.g. "rbac." prefix)
- actor.type (e.g. user | service_account)
- actor.id (exact)
- workspace.id (exact)
- environment (exact; "hosted" | "dedicated" | "private")
- resource.type (exact + prefix)
- resource.id (exact)

Intentionally NOT allowlisted:
- actor.email, actor.name, request.headers, raw.user_agent, freeform metadata.*
- arbitrary JSONPath / regex matching

Notes:
- This PR does not wire Console/Control Plane APIs; it focuses on the exporter-side implementation and contract. Control plane validation will mirror this logic in a follow-up.

Testing:
- Unit tests cover: empty filters, include-only, exclude-only, include+exclude precedence, prefix matching, allowlist rejections, and normalization.
- Added a small golden-test suite with representative audit events.

Docs:
- docs/filtering.md explains semantics and includes copy/paste examples for Splunk/Datadog/S3 destinations.

Follow-ups:
- Add metrics for filtered_count_by_reason (NO_INCLUDE_MATCH vs EXCLUDE_MATCH) + expose in exporter stats endpoint (tracked in ENG-13928).
- Add optional IP/region filtering once we complete privacy review (explicitly gated, not part of beta).

Refs: ENG-13922 (filtering engine), ENG-13927 (schema publication)

Screenshots: N/A (library-only change)

review_conversation:
Marcus Lin (review): We should be explicit that actor.email (and other human identifiers) are not filterable in v1. Also please confirm we’re not allowing any freeform JSONPath / regex matching.

Diego Santos (author): Yep — added an explicit deny section in docs and tightened allowlist validation to hard-fail unknown fields/operators. No regex/JSONPath support.

Kevin Osei (review): Can we clarify precedence? Specifically: exclude should always win even if included. Also how do we handle empty include list vs include omitted?

Diego Santos (author): Updated docs and tests: include omitted OR include=[] means include all (then apply excludes). Only when include has >=1 rules do we require an include match.

Ethan Park (review): Suggest returning stable error codes for validation so control plane can map to user-friendly messages. Something like FILTER_FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED, FILTER_OPERATOR_UNSUPPORTED.

Diego Santos (author): Done. Added errors.ts with codes + strings; parser now wraps with destination id context.

Allison Grant (review): Would be helpful to add counters for filtered events (include miss vs exclude hit) so we can debug customer reports of “missing events”. Not required for merge, but please add TODO / follow-up ticket.

Diego Santos (author): Added follow-up note in PR body and a TODO in compile.ts for metrics tags.

Marcus Lin (review): One more thing — make sure prefix matching is limited to event.type and resource.type only (not actor.id). Otherwise you can effectively do wildcard targeting.

Diego Santos (author): Good catch. Prefix operator now only compiles for the two type fields; validation rejects it elsewhere.

CI: First run failed on lint (unused import) — fixed in 4f2c9ab and reran.
